Job Title: IT Skills Demand and Employment Analysis Consultant
Job Description:
Objective of the consultancy
Sightsavers are seeking a consultant/consultancy team to conduct a skills demand and value chains analysis of the digital sector, through both interview and desk-based research. The outputs will be a report and a presentation for each respective country profile. We are looking to contract an individual consultant or consultancy team for each of the following countries: Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and Zambia.
The analysis will map out how the IT sector is organised along value chains, the types of IT jobs sustained in each IT subsector, the types and level of skills in demand for mid and entry level roles sustained in the sub-sectors and identify the barriers and catalysts to entry for employment by people with disabilities.
The specific objectives for this consultancy are:
Conduct a value chains analysis study to map the IT sector in each of the four countries (Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and Zambia).
Identify the types of jobs sustained and skills in-demand in the IT sector.
Map the barriers and catalysts which limit or promote employment and retention of young people with disabilities in the IT sector.
Validate the employment prospects and relevance of the four skill areas and propose alternatives where needed.
Responsibilities
The consultant/consultancy team will manage the primary and secondary data collection, analysis and development of the full report.
Specific tasks
Analyse the country specific IT industry, mapping the subsectors with emphasis on those that are generating jobs and have the potential to keep generating jobs in line with current market/sector trends.
Identify leading companies in each of the subsectors, map the functions that are sustained within the companies and those that are outsourced to generate an intersectoral map showing the interconnectedness. Clarity should be provided on the nature and formality of jobs sustained, such as waged employment, entrepreneurship or gig work.
Interview HR experts, CIO/CTO, tech leads and tech recruiters to identify the types of jobs sustained, level of skills required (technical and behavioural), and industry recognised certification required. Focus should be on entry and mid-level career jobs.
Interview a wide range of relevant stakeholders to establish the barriers/catalysts for young men and women with disabilities (including gendered barriers and catalysts).
Gather supplementary information from job boards to ascertain the in-demand IT jobs, levels (entry, mid, expert), required skills, experience and competences.
Interview IT instructors and educators in relevant TVET centres and training institutions to understand the most relevant curricula and accessibility challenges relevant to the inclusive teaching and learning for people with disabilities on these courses. It will also explore delivery modalities (such as in person learning or virtual class delivery), course duration, levels of certification (including recertification periods).
Analyse the data to produce an IT value chain and skills demand analysis.
Skills and Experience
The consultant/consulting team needs to possess the following requirements:
Essential:
Experience, or a Degree (Master’s or higher) in Economics, Development Studies or related field.
Professional certifications or demonstrated expertise in value chain analysis, labour market diagnostics, or skills anticipation frameworks will be an added advantage.
Extensive experience conducting sectoral studies, value chain analyses, and/or skills demand assessments, preferably in ICT or digital sectors.
Familiarity with AI and emerging technologies and its impact on jobs and digital skills development.
Strong ability to design and implement mixed-method research (quantitative and qualitative), including deploying surveys, conducting key informant interviews, and vacancy analytics.
Knowledge of local labour market dynamics, youth employment challenges, and disability inclusion is highly required.
Strong project management skills and ability to deliver within tight timelines.
Desirable:
In-depth experience of the country digital ecosystem including drivers of tech recruitment is an added advantage.
Knowledge in digital economy and labour market is desirable.

Job Summary

Prepare monthly asset and liability management (ALM) reports and circulate same to the Asset and Liability Committee (ALCO).

Ensure the adequacy of existing internal controls and risk management frameworks through continuous identification, measurement and reporting of risk positions.
Prepare the risk and control matrix for various entities within the ARM Group for the purpose of reviewing the Internal Controls over financial reporting (ICFR).
Review and update the risk appetite statements, risk measures and tolerance limits for all entities within the ARM Group.
Monitor compliance of set risk appetite measures and tolerance limits for entities within the ARM Group.
Ensure prompt reporting of risk exposures/positions and provide advice on possible resolution of critical issues.
Support automation initiatives for risk reporting and monitoring, through the use of Excel, Excel Macros, Power BI and other tools.
Engage in risk management training, workshops, town hall meetings and other form of risk awareness sessions for staff members.
Prepare comprehensive risk reports for individual risk areas as well as aggregated position for internal stakeholders, such as Senior Management and Unit Heads.
Carry out operational risk management analysis and resolution (including loss event assessment, Business Continuity assessment and others) as required from time to time.

Competency and Skills Requirements
Knowledge of the local and global financial service industry dynamics including regulations, legislations and operating environment.
Understanding of risk and return, indicators and risk management techniques as well as trading and pricing derivatives.
Ability to apply technical aspects of financial services regulation to practical business scenarios.
Knowledge of market risk concepts; knowledge of financial, systems and process audit.
Good financial accounting and budgeting skills.
Understanding of non-bank financial service operations, policies and procedures.
Problem solving and analytical abilities inclusive of statistics, data analysis and technical skills.
Minimum Qualifications
First degree in an analytical or other discipline, such as: Accounting, Economics, Finance or Engineering.
A relevant professional qualification (e.g. ACCA, ACA, CFA, FRM) and/or a Masters degree is a plus.
Maximum of three years (3) relevant experience in the financial services sector or in a related role

Company Details:
May & Baker, Nigeria Plc was founded on September 4, 1944 as Nigeria’s first pharmaceutical company. It has its origin in England, the United Kingdom where in 1834, three chemists founded Grimwade, May & Pickett, a firm for manufacturing chemicals for pharmaceutical products. In 1839...read moreGrimwade, May & Pickett transformed into May & Baker United Kingdom Limited following some changes in the ownership. May & Baker UK Limited transformed into a mega European conglomerate through a web of mergers and acquisitions over years. Consequently the name of the company has changed at different times and today, only the Nigerian offshoot is known by the original name. 

In Nigeria the company started as May & Baker (West Africa) Limited at 17A Tinubu Street, Lagos in 1944, a trading outpost to serve the West Coast of Africa. The company relocated to its present site at Ikeja, Lagos state during the Nigerian civil war. In 1976, it built its factory at Ikeja where it began local manufacturing of pharmaceuticals. That same year it changed from May & Baker (West Africa) Limited to May & Baker Nigeria Limited

In 1979, following the indigenisation decree which required that foreign interests in companies operating in Nigeria be of a minority nature, May & Baker, United Kingdom relinquished 60 per cent of its equity holding in May & Baker Nigeria to Nigerians while retaining 40 per cent. The company’s name was changed to Embechem Nigeria Limited but this was dropped later and the name reverted to May & Baker Nigeria Limited.

May & Baker Nigeria Limited became a publicly quoted company following its listing by introduction on the Nigerian Stock Exchange on November 10, 1994 and became May & Baker Nigeria Plc.

For many years expatriates sent by the parent company managed May & Baker Nigeria but in 1997, the first indigenous Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Ikemefuna Odumodu, was appointed.

In 2002 the foreign partners decided to divest. However, represented by Aventis SA, France, they remained technical associates of May & Baker Nigeria Plc. Following the merger of Aventis and Sanofi, another French firm to form Sanofi Aventis in 2004, the technical relationship transferred between May & Baker Nigeria Plc and Sanofi-Aventis of France. But that relationship was renegotiated in 2005 to give May & Baker Nigeria, the leeway to have its own products.

The company thereby began an aggressive expansion and diversification programme since 2005 which has culminated in the creation of new businesses and subsidiaries. In 2005, Biovaccines, a local vaccine production subsidiary was set up in partnership with the Federal Government of Nigeria. In 2006, the company constructed a multi-billion naira food processing factory, constructed a local plant for the production of anti-retroviral drugs in Nigeria while the construction of a World Health Organization Standard Pharmaceutical production facility was constructed and commissioned on June 27, 2011

Role Summary
The
Strategic Partnerships & Grants Officer
is a dynamic and pivotal role within the organization, responsible for driving resource mobilization, fostering impactful collaborations, and ensuring the successful acquisition and management of grants. This position combines strategic thinking, relationship building, and excellent project management skills to enhance the organization’s sustainability and programmatic reach.
The officer will identify funding opportunities, cultivate donor and partner relationships, and oversee grant applications and compliance processes. They will also serve as the organization’s representative in building alliances, promoting its mission, and working collaboratively with internal teams to align grants and partnerships with strategic objectives.
By integrating grant management and partnership development, this role ensures that BFFWH has the resources, networks, and collaborative support needed to address critical women’s health challenges and achieve its mission.
Key Responsibilities:
Grant Management
Grant Identification and Research:
Continuously research and identify new grant opportunities aligned with the organization’s mission.
Maintain a database of prospective funding opportunities and timelines.
Proposal Development:
Write and submit high-quality grant proposals, tailored to meet specific donor requirements.
Collaborate with program teams to develop compelling project descriptions, budgets, and measurable outcomes.
Grant Compliance and Reporting:
Ensure timely and accurate reporting to donors, including financial reports, project updates, and impact assessments.
Develop and monitor grant agreements to ensure compliance with donor regulations and organizational policies.
Relationship Management with Funders:
Cultivate and maintain relationships with grant-making organizations, including foundations, government agencies, and institutional donors.
Act as the primary point of contact for existing funders, responding promptly to inquiries and providing regular updates.
Partnership Development
Stakeholder Engagement:
Build and maintain relationships with strategic partners, including NGOs, governmental bodies, corporate organizations, and academic institutions.
Represent the organization at networking events, conferences, and meetings to promote its mission and programs.
Collaboration Opportunities:
Identify and pursue potential partnership opportunities to expand program reach, leverage resources, and enhance impact.
Develop Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) and other agreements to formalize collaborations.
Advocacy and Alliances:
Coordinate with advocacy teams to engage partners in joint campaigns or initiatives.
Build coalitions to address key women’s health challenges, particularly those impacting reproductive health and fistula patients.
Resource Mobilization and Diversification
Diversified Funding Strategies:
Develop strategies to diversify the organization’s funding sources, including corporate sponsorships, private donations, and institutional grants.
Explore innovative fundraising approaches, such as cause marketing, crowdfunding, and social enterprise partnerships.
Donor Stewardship:
Organize donor appreciation events, site visits, and recognition campaigns to enhance donor loyalty.
Work closely with the communications team to showcase impact stories and engage donors through newsletters and social media.
Strategic Planning and Data Management
Strategic Alignment:
Work with leadership to align grant applications and partnership goals with the organization’s strategic plan.
Contribute to long-term sustainability planning by identifying trends in funding and partnership opportunities.
Monitoring and Evaluation:
Collaborate with M&E teams to develop metrics and tools to measure the impact of grants and partnerships.
Use data to demonstrate program effectiveness and communicate value to stakeholders.
Knowledge Management:
Maintain a centralized repository of grant applications, partnership agreements, and donor communications for institutional memory.
Document lessons learned from grant applications and partnerships to improve future initiatives.

Additional Responsibilities:
Stay updated on global and regional trends in philanthropy, donor priorities, and public health challenges affecting women.
Ensure ethical practices in fundraising and partnership development, adhering to transparency and accountability standards.

Proven track record of securing and managing grants from institutional donors, foundations, and international agencies.

Experience in donor engagement and relationship management, including corporate social responsibility (CSR) partnerships.

Exceptional ability to develop compelling, data-driven proposals and applications tailored to donor requirements.

Strong interpersonal and communication skills to build and sustain effective partnerships with donors, government agencies, and stakeholders.

Proficiency in coordinating multiple projects, ensuring timelines, deliverables, and donor expectations are met.
Research and Analytical Skills:
Capacity to identify funding opportunities, analyze donor trends, and generate insights to enhance proposals and partnerships.

Basic knowledge of budgeting, financial reporting, and resource allocation for grant and partnership activities.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly and persuasively.
Team Collaboration:
Ability to work cross-functionally with program teams, finance, and leadership to align grant and partnership initiatives.

Strong organizational skills to manage deadlines, documentation, and compliance with donor expectations.
Adaptability:
Flexibility to navigate a fast-paced environment and respond to emerging opportunities or challenges.
Technology Proficiency:
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and donor management software.
Experience using project management tools (e.g., Trello, Asana) and CRM platforms.
Familiarity with online grant application portals and reporting platforms.

Job Description:
Position Summary
The Medical Director plays a foundational role in the establishment and launch of the clinic. This position is responsible for overseeing clinical operations, leading the development of comprehensive clinical protocols and workflows, and ensuring the delivery of safe, ethical, and high-quality patient care. The Medical Director ensures that all clinical services align with applicable Nigerian healthcare regulations and are responsive to community needs.
Foundational Collaboration & Local Presence
This is a founding, on-site leadership position requiring close, daily collaboration with the Clinic Manager
This role requires physical presence in Akure, Ondo State and active participation in pre-opening planning, staff training, and clinic readiness activities
Candidates must be available to begin work approximately 6–8 weeks prior to the planned clinic opening in June 2026 to support foundational setup and system development.
This position is not remote
Key Responsibilities
Clinic Establishment & Clinical Protocol Development
Lead the development, documentation, and implementation of comprehensive clinical protocols, workflows, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all services offered by the clinic
Ensure clinical protocols align with applicable Nigerian healthcare regulations and standards, including guidelines issued by the Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH), National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA), Ondo State Ministry of Health, and relevant Local Government Area health authorities
Support clinic licensing, inspections, and readiness for operational launch
Participate in phased service rollout planning and service expansion
Work in close partnership with the Clinic Manager to ensure clinical protocols are operationally feasible, compliant, and sustainable
Clinical Oversight & Workflow Design
Design, implement, and oversee clinical workflows for:
Adult primary care services
Gynecologic and reproductive health services
Pediatric and well-baby care
Routine and expanded vaccination services
Antenatal (prenatal) care
Malaria and HIV care
Minor injury care
Adapt workflows to staffing capacity, available resources, and local community needs
Support continuous improvement of care delivery systems
Patient Care Coordination
Serve as a liaison between patients, clinical staff, and healthcare providers to ensure continuity and quality of care
Establish referral and escalation pathways for cases requiring higher-level or specialized care
Promote patient-centered and culturally appropriate care
Medical Equipment Oversight
Contribute to the selection, distribution, and appropriate use of medical equipment
Establish equipment usage protocols and maintenance schedules
Collaborate with clinic management on equipment procurement and replacement planning
Compliance, Quality & Training
Ensure implementation of infection prevention and control (IPC) protocols
Support training of clinical staff on SOPs, patient safety, and quality standards
Participate in audits, inspections, and quality improvement initiatives
Required Qualifications
Registered Nurse (RN) qualification recognized in Nigeria
Minimum of 5 years of experience in outpatient or primary healthcare settings
Experience contributing to clinical workflow or protocol development
Strong understanding of Nigerian primary healthcare delivery systems
Demonstrated leadership, communication, and organizational skills
Computer and electronic health record system literacy
Preferred Qualifications
Experience establishing or scaling healthcare services
Prior involvement in SOP or clinical protocol development
Experience in maternal and child health services
Compensation & Benefits
Monthly compensation range: ₦200,000 – ₦250,000, commensurate with experience, qualifications, and scope of responsibility
The upper end of the range reflects the expected compensation for a fully qualified candidate taking on full clinical leadership and protocol development responsibilities
This is a founding leadership role, and compensation reflects the added responsibility of clinic establishment and pre-launch work
Benefits and additional allowances (if applicable) will be discussed with shortlisted candidates as the clinic’s benefits structure is finalized
Application Requirements
Interested candidates should submit the following:
A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV)
Contact information for two professional references (references will only be contacted for shortlisted candidates)
A brief outline (1–2 pages maximum) describing your proposed approach to establishing clinical practice at the Julayo clinic, including:
Clinical workflow structure for primary care services
Patient care coordination systems
Quality assurance and infection prevention practices
Referral pathways and escalation procedures
Any additional considerations you believe are essential for safe and effective service delivery in Akure
The outline is intended to understand your thinking and leadership approach; it does not need to be a fully developed operational document.
Application Timeline & Hiring Process
Applications will be accepted for a period of four (4) weeks from the date of posting
Candidates will be contacted shortly after the application deadline to be informed of next steps
Interviews are expected to be completed within two weeks following the closing date
Final selection and hiring decisions will be made promptly thereafter
The selected candidate is expected to begin work approximately 6–8 weeks prior to clinic opening in June 2026, allowing sufficient time for collaborative planning and clinic establishment activities
Hiring will be finalized in advance of key leadership transition and site preparation activities scheduled for May 2026 to ensure continuity of planning and execution
